opportunities.name: Plan a city trip (flight + hotel + tour) and log it to notes
opportunities.description: For a given destination and date range, search round-trip flights from Paris on Google Flights, find a hotel on Booking.com, find a tour of a named attraction on Viator, then save a trip summary note with the prices.
steps: On Google Flights, set origin to Paris and destination to {destination}
Open the Departure date picker and select {depart_date} and {return_date}, click Done, then search
Read off the cheapest or preferred flight (airline, price)
On Booking.com, enter {destination} as the destination and choose the matching suggestion
Select check-in {depart_date} and check-out {return_date}, then click Search
Open the chosen hotel and note its name and total price
On Viator, search '{attraction} tour {destination}' and open the top tour, noting its name and price
In Notes, create a new note: 'Trip {destination} {dates}: flight {airline} {price}, hotel {hotel} {price}, {attraction} tour: {tour_name} {price}'

instances.values: Rome, Dec 3–7 2026, Colosseum; easyJet €89, Room Roma Nazionale €452, Colosseum tour €54
Barcelona, Jan 20–24 2027, Sagrada Familia; Vueling-Iberia €113, IBIS BUDGET BARCELONA CENTER €543, Sagrada Familia tour €54

opportunities.name: Look up browser support for a web feature and email the answer
opportunities.description: For a given web feature and browser, check the support version on caniuse, find the MDN docs page, then write an email reply to a colleague with the minimum supported version and the docs link.
steps: On caniuse.com, clear the search box and type {feature}, then press Enter
Read off the first version of {browser} that supports it
On MDN, click 'Search the site', search for {feature}, and open the matching reference page; copy its URL
In mail, compose a message To {recipient_email}
Set Subject to 'Re: {feature} in {browser}'
Set Body to 'Hi {name}, {feature} is supported in {browser} from version {version}. Docs: {mdn_url}'
Send (or discard/save the draft)

opportunities.name: Compare two Python packages on PyPI and record a note
opportunities.description: For a pair of Python packages, open each one's PyPI page and source repository to collect latest version, release date, GitHub stars and license, then save a one-line comparison note.
steps: On PyPI, search for {package_a} and press Enter
Open the package result; note the latest version and release date
Click the Source/Repository link; note the star count and license
Repeat the search, project page and repository steps for {package_b}
In Notes, create a new note: '{a} {version} {date} {stars} stars {license} vs {b} {version} {date} {stars} stars {license}'
